record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) handle high-mobility users in ultra-dense networks when user-centric access-point clusters, channel state information acquisition, synchronization, calibration, scheduling, and fronthaul routing may all need to adapt quickly as users move?

evidence.quote: In addition to the key questions addressed in this paper, there are still many interesting research questions requiring future comprehensive studies, such as 1) At what level of densification is CF-MMIMO truly beneficial? When is it not really needed?; 2) How to handle high mobility in UDNs with CF-MMIMO?
It is fundamentally difficult in pCell, or any such CF-MMIMO system, to support substantial mobility, given the CSI and user-centered synchronization requirements.
But these clusters change quickly with user load and locations. This requires more control signaling and poses a huge challenge.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open research direction for ultra-dense cell-free massive MIMO systems. Recent surveys and research papers on CF-MMIMO continue to list high-mobility support, dynamic user-centric clustering, and rapid CSI/synchronization adaptation as unresolved challenges; no comprehensive solution with provable scalable guarantees has been established.
